predecessors.name: Kahuripan
predecessors.text: the western half of Kahuripan, the share of one of Airlangga's two sons

successors.name: Singhasari
successors.text: the whole kingdom after the Battle of Ganter: 'Kediri became a fief under the kingdom of Singasari'

successors.name: Majapahit
successors.text: Jayakatwang's restored kingdom, ended by 'attacks by Yuan and Raden Wijaya's forces'; Majapahit's first king was enthroned on 12 November 1293

ledger.x: 1045: Kediri (Panjalu) arises in the partition of Kahuripan.
1049: civil war between Janggala and Panjalu after Airlangga's death.
1052: the civil war with Janggala ends.
1135: Kediri moves on Janggala under Jayabaya.
1136: the contest ends in a union of the crowns.
1222: Kertajaya loses to Ken Arok at Ganter and Kediri becomes a fief of Singhasari.
1292: Jayakatwang restores Kediri by overthrowing Singhasari.
1293: Jayakatwang's Kediri falls and Majapahit follows.

wars.name: Janggala-Panjalu civil war
wars.outcome: Fighting between the two halves of Kahuripan after Airlangga's death; no victor and no change of frontier given.

wars.name: Kediri's absorption of Janggala under Jayabaya
wars.outcome: Janggala is taken over by Kediri and ceases to exist with the 1136 marriage of Kameswara to a Janggala princess.

wars.name: Battle of Ganter (Tumapel conquest of Kediri)
wars.outcome: Ken Arok of Tumapel defeats Kertajaya; Kediri becomes a fief of the new kingdom of Singhasari.

wars.name: Jayakatwang's revolt and the Yuan invasion of Java
wars.outcome: Jayakatwang kills Kertanagara in 1292 and rules Kediri for about a year; Mongol ships arrive near Tuban in early 1293, Raden Vijaya forces them out on 31 May 1293 and founds Majapahit.

certainty.note: No page gives a boundary for Kediri; the only line is the legend of a river made by Mpu Bharada's water between Kediri and Janggala.
